references.text: Parallel list of unclean birds in the Mosaic Law, which also mentions the stork as an unclean bird that Israelites were not to eat
The complete list of unclean birds in Leviticus corresponding to the list in Deuteronomy 14, including herons, the hawk, and the bat
The stork is mentioned here in connection with its building nests in cypress trees, illustrating the bird's natural habitat
The stork is described as a bird that knows its appointed times, in contrast to God's people who lack knowledge of His ways
The stork is used as an image in Zechariah's vision, where women with wings like those of a stork carry an ephah container
